shows.name: the Cheshire Show
shows.where: on the green off the market square in Macclesfield
shows.blurb: Prize cheeses, a dog show, and a tug of war the farmers take far too seriously.

shows.name: the Royal Welsh Show
shows.blurb: It's usually in Llanelwedd, but the sheep fancied a change of scenery and nobody argues with the sheep.

shows.name: the Great Yorkshire Show
shows.where: on the green inside the north walls at York
shows.blurb: Shire horses the size of sheds, and a man selling the best pork pie in the county. He'll tell you so.

shows.name: the Royal Highland Show
shows.where: on the green at the south end of Edinburgh
shows.blurb: Highland cattle with better fringes than yours, and a pipe band that starts at nine sharp.

shows.name: the Balmoral Show
shows.where: on the top lawn at the north-west corner of Belfast
shows.blurb: Ulster's biggest day out: sheepdogs, soda bread and the finest tractors money can polish.

shows.name: the Ploughing
shows.where: on the green by the railway in Galway
shows.blurb: The National Ploughing Championships have ploughed into Galway this year. Straight furrows, wellies, and a hundred thousand people talking about the weather.

plaques.produce: Plaque on the produce tent: Allotments are older than most people think. The Small Holdings and Allotments Act of 1908 made councils in England and Wales provide them, and in the Second World War the Dig for Victory campaign put a great many more under the spade. Size counts, but the judges mark condition just as hard: a giant marrow with a split skin goes home with nothing.
plaques.sheepdog: Plaque by the sheepdog pen: The first recorded sheepdog trials were held at Bala, in Wales, in 1873. Nearly every working border collie today descends from Old Hemp, a dog born in Northumberland in 1893. Good handlers say the trick is to keep calm, because the sheep can always tell.
